Market Intelligence Briefing
subheadings: 🇺🇸 United States  Mixed  on hold / consumer softening
🇪🇺 European Union  Bullish  on hold / easing bias
🇨🇳 China  Mixed  easing support / weak demand
🇯🇵 Japan  Bullish  fiscal push / yen strength
🇦🇺 Australia  Mixed  hawkish RBA / strong AUD
🧮 Earnings Pattern — What the Market Pays For
Turnarounds and capital returns are paid; consumer misses are not
🔍 Underowned Themes — Active on X, Underweight in Portfolios
US natural gas: the overlooked power input
ETF inflows return, but crypto activity is drying up
Bull steepening, weaker dollar, record debt issuance
🔮 Anticipatory Positioning — Markets Pricing In Future Events
CJEU WIBOR ruling and Polish banks
Robinhood / HOOD  "prediction markets vs. crypto drought"
Gold and silver / GLD, SLV  "'all greed, no fear'"
Hims & Hers / HIMS  "the GLP-1 trade gets real"
body: Wednesday, February 11 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: The consumer is cooling: December retail sales stalled, with Reuters flagging underlying weakness Reuters [Feb 10]. The Fed is not reacting yet; Cleveland's Hammack says rates could be on hold 'for quite some time' Reuters [Feb 10]. Softer demand plus a patient Fed argues for lower front-end yields and a weaker dollar, not a growth scare in equities, unless payrolls crack.

Rates & Curve: The 2Y closed at 3.45% and the 10Y at 4.16%, a 10Y−2Y spread of 71 bps; over 20 observations the 2Y fell 9 bps and the 10Y 3 bps, and over five observations both fell 12 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-10). The curve is moderately steep, approaching the long-run average, and the 20-observation move is a bull steepening (both down, 2Y down more). The S&P 500 closed at 6,941.81, down 0.33%, with the VIX at 17.79 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

New / Most Important: The delayed January jobs report is released Wednesday, with inflation data also on this week's slate CNBC [Feb 10] Investopedia [Feb 08]. The White House is already seeking to downplay any slowdown The New York Times [Feb 10]. Under the surface, Wall Street's anything-but-tech trade is reshaping the market: the Dow closed at 50,188.14 while the Nasdaq 100 is down 2.56% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10) Financial Times [Feb 10].

Playbook ✓: Own 2Y Treasuries and the bull steepener into payrolls; keep equity exposure in industrials, energy and materials rather than mega-cap tech or discretionary. Change the call if payrolls surprise strongly and the 2Y retraces above 3.54%, its level 20 observations ago (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-10).

Macro Stance: The ECB kept rates steady and shrugged off the inflation dip, but its own research now argues that foreign import tariffs mean lower inflation and weaker activity for the euro area Reuters [Feb 05] European Central Bank [Feb 10]. With inflation at 1.7% in January, the next move is more likely a cut than a hike Financial Times [Feb 04].

Activity & Inflation: EUR/USD closed at 1.1904, up 0.66% in the prior session and 2.03% over 20 sessions, an extra disinflationary force (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). The STOXX 600 closed at 620.97, up 1.72% over 20 sessions, while the DAX is down 1.7% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

New / Most Important: Company results are carrying Europe: Philips surged 12% on a clear step-up in sales even as European stocks closed down, Kering jumped 12% as its new CEO mapped a revival, and Barclays beat and plans to return £15bn to investors CNBC [Feb 10] CNBC [Feb 10] Yahoo Finance UK [Feb 10]. Turnaround stories with capital returns are being paid.

Playbook ✓: Overweight European banks, insurers and quality cyclicals with self-help stories; fund from US mega-cap tech. Add Bund duration on back-ups. Avoid German autos and exporters most exposed to a strong euro. Change the call if EUR/USD gains force a growth downgrade or if AI-disruption selling spreads further into European financials.

Macro Stance: Policy is leaning toward support while demand stays weak. The PBOC promised financial support to boost domestic demand, and Beijing is tightening market oversight to engineer a 'slow bull' in equities Reuters [Feb 10] Reuters [Feb 10]. Real activity has not turned, so we stay Mixed: own policy-backed equities and the currency, avoid consumption-exposed cyclicals.

PMIs & Activity: The latest official manufacturing PMI, for January, dropped to 49.3, in contraction Reuters [Jan 30]. The new hard data point is worse: China's auto sales fell at the fastest pace in nearly two years in January Reuters [Feb 10]. Confirmation of a turn would need the February official PMI back above 50 and a stabilisation in car sales once trade-in subsidies kick in.

Credit Impulse: The feed carries no January credit or aggregate financing print yet. The signal is policy intent: the PBOC's pledge of financial support for domestic demand points to targeted relending rather than broad rate cuts Reuters [Feb 10]. Regulators are also urging banks to curb exposure to US Treasuries, which keeps more liquidity onshore Bloomberg.com [Feb 08]. We treat the impulse as modestly positive pending the data.

Property: The Shenzhen government is drafting an $11.6 billion rescue package for China Vanke, according to Octus Reuters [Feb 10]. That is the clearest sign yet that local governments will backstop large developers rather than let them fail, but S&P still expects the property slump to be worse than it previously forecast this year CNBC [Feb 09]. Credit risk is falling faster than sales are recovering, so prefer developer bonds over equity, and watch whether other cities copy Shenzhen.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: China plans to invest 5 trillion yuan in its power grid over the next 5 years, a direct support for grid equipment, cables and copper demand China Daily Global Edition [Feb 10]. Fiscal policy otherwise stays targeted rather than broad, favouring infrastructure over household transfers. On trade, Europe is debating a 'mega tariff': a French minister urged caution amid calls for a 30% duty on Chinese goods South China Morning Post [Feb 10]. That keeps Chinese exporters' European growth at risk just as US access narrows.

Markets & Flows: The Hang Seng closed at 27,183.15, up 1.25% over 20 sessions, and the Shanghai Composite at 4,128.37, down 0.25% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). ASHR closed at 34.03 and KWEB at 34.31, down 8.9% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). USD/CNY closed at 6.9220, down 0.24% in the prior session and 0.73% over 20 sessions, extending the yuan's run (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). Chinese stocks won the most MSCI index additions in nearly three years Bloomberg.com [Feb 10].

New / Most Important: The MSCI additions and the 'slow bull' oversight push matter most for flows: passive money is being pulled into A-shares just as regulators try to dampen volatility Bloomberg.com [Feb 10] Reuters [Feb 10]. The Vanke rescue reduces tail risk in the property chain Reuters [Feb 10].

Playbook ✓: Own CNY strength and A-share index exposure via ASHR, plus grid-equipment and copper beneficiaries of the 5 trillion yuan plan China Daily Global Edition [Feb 10]; avoid Hong Kong internet, with KWEB down 8.9% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10), and auto makers. Change the call if the January credit data disappoint or the yuan reverses. ⚠ Divergence: Beijing is adding support and index inclusion is pulling in money, yet auto sales just fell at the fastest pace in nearly two years Reuters [Feb 10]; the equity bid is running ahead of the real economy.

Macro Stance: Takaichi's LDP holds a two-thirds supermajority in the Lower House, giving her room for fiscal stimulus The Japan Times [Feb 09]. The domestic economy is not uniformly strong: business bankruptcies hit a 13-year high in January as costs bite The Japan Times [Feb 10].

Activity & Currency: The Nikkei 225 closed at a record 57,650.54, up 2.28% in the prior session and 7.66% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). USD/JPY closed at 156.13, down 0.71% in the prior session and 1.17% over 20 sessions, as the yen extended a winning streak after dour US data (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10) Reuters [Feb 10].

Playbook ✓: Stay long Japanese equities, tilted to banks, defence and domestic reflation, and let the yen hedge run off as the currency strengthens; a record Nikkei alongside a firmer yen means foreign investors are earning on both legs. Change the call if super-long JGB yields spike on spending plans, if USD/JPY reverses above 157.99, its level 20 sessions ago (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10), or if the yen's rise starts to hit exporter guidance.

Macro Stance: Deputy Governor Hauser warned that inflation is 'too high' and the RBA cannot let it persist, so the hiking bias stays Bloomberg.com [Feb 10]. Australia's banks are thriving in that setting: CBA's first-half earnings hit a record on market share gains and the shares surged Reuters [Feb 10].

Demand & Financing: AUD/USD closed at 0.7084, up 5.6% over 20 sessions, tightening conditions for exporters (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). The ASX 200 closed at 8,867.40, down 0.5% in the prior session and up 1.23% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). CSL plunged to an eight-year low after its CEO departed and earnings disappointed CNBC [Feb 10].

Playbook ✓: Own the major banks and resources; avoid offshore earners such as CSL whose translated profits suffer from the strong AUD. With the currency up 5.6% over 20 sessions and the RBA still hawkish, domestic financial conditions are tightening on two fronts (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). Change the call if the RBA turns cautious after its growth warning or if bank margins come under pressure from deposit competition.

Monetary & Activity: Fitch warned that Poland risks a rating downgrade if its debt is not stabilised, the first serious fiscal flag of the year Reuters [Feb 10]. The offset is cheap defence funding: EU ambassadors approved a €44bn loan for Poland under the SAFE programme polskieradio.pl [Feb 10]. Monetary policy remains on pause, with the NBP projecting inflation in line with target and key decisions flagged for March Business Insider Polska [Feb 06]; a March cut would support domestic equities and bonds.

FX & Markets: USD/PLN closed at 3.5332, down 0.88% in the prior session and 2.08% over 20 sessions, and EUR/PLN at 4.2055 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). EPOL closed at 38.11, down 1.68% in the prior session but up 4.76% over 20 sessions, and the WIG20TR tracker at 67.56 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). KGHM fell 5.17% in the prior session and 10.41% over five, while Pekao is up 9.67% and Orlen 11.42% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

Companies: Money.pl reports Orlen shares at their highest in years as commodities drive profits Money.pl [Feb 10]. Dino's governance problem is escalating: instead of the board, lawyers turned up to a meeting with unions, Bankier reports Bankier.pl [Feb 10]. Dino is down 8.72% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

Security & New Development: Warsaw denied involvement in the assassination attempt on a Russian general TVP World [Feb 10]. The binary event is the EU Court of Justice ruling on WIBOR on 12 February, which Bankier frames as a possible breakthrough for borrowers Bankier.pl [Feb 09]. PKO BP is down 4.08% over five sessions into the ruling (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

Playbook ✓: Stay overweight Poland via EPOL with a tilt to Orlen and defence-adjacent names funded by SAFE polskieradio.pl [Feb 10]; stay underweight banks into the WIBOR ruling and avoid Dino. ⚠ Divergence: the zloty keeps strengthening while Fitch warns of a downgrade Reuters [Feb 10]; if the fiscal story gains traction, FX and bonds would reprice before equities.

Narrative: The debate has moved from 'sell software' to 'which software survives': JPMorgan says the historic software selloff has gone far enough and lists stocks to buy on sale CNBC [Feb 10]. XLK closed at 142.55, down 2.89% over 20 sessions, with Microsoft down 13.39% and Oracle 21.88% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

Reported: No large-cap software name reported in the session; the group traded on strategist calls rather than results. Oracle rose 2.11% while Palantir fell 2.38% and is down 22.24% over 20 sessions, showing that even AI winners are not immune to the de-rating (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

EPS Upside Watch: Networking: Cisco unveiled a new AI networking chip to take on Broadcom and Nvidia, and reports this week Reuters [Feb 10] Investopedia [Feb 08]. AI-networking orders are the cleanest route to an upside surprise for hardware vendors outside the GPU trade.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The AI-disruption trade is now spreading from software to financials, as the WSJ reports WSJ [Feb 10]. That rotation of fear may mark the late stage of the software sell-off, the point where the best-quality names can be bought.

Narrative: Capex is now funded with century debt: Alphabet sold a rare 100-year bond to fund AI expansion as spending surges Reuters [Feb 10]. XLC closed at 117.58, flat over 20 sessions, while GOOGL fell 1.77% in the prior session and 4% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).
Reported: Spotify jumped on strong earnings and subscriber growth WSJ [Feb 10]. Disney rose 2.64% and Netflix 0.91% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

EPS Upside Watch: Subscription platforms with pricing power: Spotify's beat shows that engagement plus price increases still compounds earnings, and Meta at 670.72, up 4.48% over 20 sessions, remains the ad-led leader (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

⚡ Breaking Convention: A 100-year bond from a tech platform tells you balance sheets, not cash flows, are now funding the AI race Reuters [Feb 10]. Equity investors should demand a higher return on Alphabet's capex, which is why the stock lags despite record demand for its debt.

Narrative: The AI threat has widened to the financial sector: wealth managers, brokers and insurers are being sold on fears that AI tools will compress fees WSJ [Feb 10]. XLF closed at 53.55, down 3.15% over 20 sessions, with BAC down 1.81% and JPM 1.19% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

Reported: Barclays beat profit estimates and plans to return £15bn to investors Yahoo Finance UK [Feb 10]. Good results are not enough to protect US financials when the multiple, not earnings, is being questioned.

EPS Upside Watch: Big balance-sheet banks with trading and underwriting exposure: Goldman closed at 948.99, roughly flat over 20 sessions, as debt issuance booms (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). They benefit from record bond deals like Alphabet's Reuters [Feb 10].

⚡ Breaking Convention: Morgan Stanley warns the AI-led software selloff may pose a risk for the $1.5 trillion US credit market tied to software Reuters [Feb 10]. If that risk crystallises, banks with direct lending books and BDCs are the transmission channel; stay underweight brokers, wealth managers and alternative lenders.

Narrative: Energy remains the rotation leader: XLE closed at 53.58, up 15.62% over 20 sessions, with XOM up 22.22% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). Brent closed at 68.80, up 7.72% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

Reported: BP suspended its share buyback plan in a fresh sign of oil-price pressure CNBC [Feb 10]. European majors are cutting distributions while US integrateds with lower costs keep theirs, so the US names are the better expression of the sector.

EPS Upside Watch: Exxon and Chevron: XOM's 22.22% and CVX's 12.27% gains over 20 sessions show the market already pricing better first-quarter numbers (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). Upside depends on Brent holding its 20-session gain.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Trump hinted at sending a second carrier to the Middle East as Iran and the US near talks, so the geopolitical premium can rise even while diplomacy continues Reuters [Feb 10]. Keep upstream exposure; the risk premium is not fully priced at a Brent of 68.80 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

Narrative: Industrials are holding the rotation: XLI closed at 173.91, up 6.58% over 20 sessions, with Caterpillar up 17.88% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). The anything-but-tech trade is pulling capital into machinery, defence and grid names Financial Times [Feb 10].
Reported: Kongsberg's results showed defence execution and a record backlog, and Morningstar raised its fair value estimate Morningstar [Feb 10]. Defence order books keep translating into upgrades.

EPS Upside Watch: Grid and power equipment: China's 5 trillion yuan grid plan adds to US data-centre demand for transformers and cables China Daily Global Edition [Feb 10]. Suppliers with exposure to both markets have the strongest estimate momentum.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Boeing is down 0.87% in the prior session and GE Aerospace 2.42% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10): aerospace is lagging the cycle trade even as defence and machinery lead. Rotate within the sector rather than out of it.

Narrative: The consumer is slowing, as the FT puts it, and December retail sales stalled Financial Times [Feb 10] Reuters [Feb 10]. XLY closed at 118.33, down 4.97% over 20 sessions, and AMZN is down 16.03% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

Reported: Ford reported its worst quarterly earnings miss in four years while guiding for a better 2026 CNBC [Feb 10]. Misses are clustering where consumers can defer purchases, and big-ticket goods are the first to feel a stalling consumer.

EPS Upside Watch: Home Depot rose 2.28% in the prior session and is up 3.93% over 20 sessions, while Tesla rose 1.89% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). Housing repair is the one area where lower yields could lift estimates; Nike, down 3.96% over 20 sessions, still lacks a demand catalyst (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Stock prices and consumer reality are diverging: the market has priced a soft landing while the December sales data show stalling demand Reuters [Feb 10]. Stay underweight until payrolls show the labour market is holding.

Narrative: Staples' rotation premium is being tested: XLP closed at 87.15, still up 8.69% over 20 sessions, but Costco fell 2.64% and Walmart 1.8% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).
Reported: Coca-Cola forecast modest growth amid demand concerns CNBC [Feb 10]. Even the highest-quality brands are struggling to push volume, and pricing alone no longer carries the growth algorithm.

EPS Upside Watch: Upside is limited to companies with pricing power and a value tilt; WMT is still up 7.4% over 20 sessions on share gains (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). Discount and warehouse formats keep taking share from branded manufacturers when volume growth stalls, so retailers beat suppliers in this phase.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The defensive bid assumed staples were immune to a slowing consumer; Coca-Cola's demand warning says otherwise CNBC [Feb 10]. Trim crowded mega-cap staples and keep only the share gainers.
Narrative: Healthcare is lagging the rotation: XLV closed at 155.33, down 1.3% over 20 sessions, with LLY down 5.18% and UNH 19.76% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).
Reported: CVS beat estimates, but the stock fell Barron's [Feb 10]. The market wants more than a beat from managed care; it wants evidence that medical-cost trends have peaked.

EPS Upside Watch: Pharmacy-benefit and retail-pharmacy turnarounds such as CVS can surprise upward if medical-cost trends stabilise. Lilly at 1,025.00 is down 5.18% over 20 sessions, leaving room for upside if GLP-1 demand stays strong (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

⚡ Breaking Convention: A stock falling on a beat is a sign of capitulation rather than fresh bad news Barron's [Feb 10]. Begin accumulating managed care on weakness; UNH at 273.22 already prices a lot of risk (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

Narrative: Materials are the second-best sector of the rotation: XLB closed at 52.91, up 9.05% over 20 sessions and 1.4% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). Gold closed at 5,031.00, up 9.02% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).
Reported: No major US materials name reported in the session; gold miners held up, with Newmont rising 0.66% even as gold slipped 0.95% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

EPS Upside Watch: Gold producers: with gold up 9.02% over 20 sessions, miners' margins expand faster than their costs, and Newmont is up 7.59% over the same window (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). Copper supply is tight too: production at Codelco's El Teniente will stay at a lower level for the next 5 years Reuters [Feb 10].

⚡ Breaking Convention: Copper fell 0.82% in the prior session to 5.90 even as Codelco signalled years of lower output (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10) Reuters [Feb 10]. Supply disruption, not demand, is the driver for the AI data-centre and grid metal, so dips are buying opportunities.

Narrative: REITs are the cleanest beneficiary of the bull steepening: XLRE closed at 42.84, up 1.4% in the prior session and 5.47% over 20 sessions, as the 10Y fell 12 bps over five observations (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10; US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-10).
Reported: The feed window carries no major US REIT result; the group traded on rates as the 10Y fell to 4.16% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-10).

EPS Upside Watch: Data-centre landlords and healthcare REITs with contracted rent growth carry the best FFO upside, and lower yields reduce refinancing costs across the group. The 30Y at 4.78%, down 5 bps over 20 observations, eases the cost of long-dated property debt (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-10).
⚡ Breaking Convention: REITs are rallying on the same weak data that hurts discretionary stocks; a strong payrolls print would reverse the move fast. Own them as a rates trade, not a growth trade.
Narrative: Utilities are working again: XLU closed at 44.20, up 1.66% in the prior session and 3.8% over 20 sessions, with Vistra up 4.33% and NextEra 1.51% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).
Reported: No large US utility reported in the session; the group traded on lower yields and data-centre demand.
EPS Upside Watch: Regulated utilities with data-centre load growth gain from lower funding costs; NEE is up 11.97% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Merchant power is bouncing but has not repaired the damage: Vistra rose 4.33% in the prior session yet is down 7.52% over 20 sessions, and Constellation is down 19.27% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). Political pressure over data-centre power costs caps merchant upside; own regulated names and treat merchant rallies as exits.

Narrative: Germany's auto lobby says the industry is in 'crisis' as investment and jobs move abroad Reuters [Feb 10]. The SXAP tracker bounced 2.46% in the prior session but is down 1.66% over 20 sessions, and STLA is down 28.42% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

Reported: Honda's third-quarter profit slumped over 60% as EV restructuring bit Reuters [Feb 10]. EV write-downs are spreading across global producers, and European mass-market makers have the least room to absorb them.

EPS Upside Watch: Volkswagen is the relative winner: VOW3 rose 3.62% in the prior session and is up 2.4% over 20 sessions, while BMW rose 1.18% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). Scale in EVs gives VW more room to protect margins than mass-market peers.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The bounce is relief, not recovery: a German industry describing itself as in crisis does not support a re-rating Reuters [Feb 10]. Sell rallies in mass-market names; Volkswagen is the only relative long.

Narrative: TSMC's board approved a record $45 billion spending package on new fabs, the strongest capex signal in the chain Tom's Hardware [Feb 10]. SOXX closed at 351.43, up 6.38% over 20 sessions, and TSM at 361.91, up 1.83% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

Reported: SMIC reported a 60.7% increase in fourth-quarter profit, showing China's foundry demand is booming as well Reuters [Feb 10]. Intel fell 6.19% and Micron 2.67% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

EPS Upside Watch: Memory: Bloomberg says the memory chip squeeze is wreaking havoc in markets, with more to come Bloomberg.com [Feb 10]. Pricing power favours memory makers; MU is still up 7.92% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The same memory squeeze that lifts producers hurts every downstream hardware maker's margins Bloomberg.com [Feb 10]. Own foundry and memory, avoid PC and handset chip designers.

Rewarded: Self-help and capital returns: Kering jumped 12% as its new CEO mapped a revival, Philips surged 12% on a step-up in sales, Barclays plans to return £15bn, and Spotify jumped on subscriber growth CNBC [Feb 10] CNBC [Feb 10] Yahoo Finance UK [Feb 10] WSJ [Feb 10]. CBA's record half lifted its shares Reuters [Feb 10].

Punished: Consumer and AI-exposed misses: Ford posted its worst miss in four years, Coca-Cola forecast only modest growth, CVS fell despite a beat, and Robinhood's revenue disappointed on a crypto slowdown CNBC [Feb 10] CNBC [Feb 10] Barron's [Feb 10] Reuters [Feb 10]. CSL plunged to an eight-year low CNBC [Feb 10].

Pattern: The market pays for internal catalysts it can underwrite — a new CEO, a cost plan, a buyback — and punishes anything that depends on the consumer or on crypto volumes. Beats without raised guidance are sold.

Attention into EPS: Cisco and McDonald's report alongside the delayed jobs and inflation data Investopedia [Feb 08]. Coinbase also has earnings this week, after JPMorgan cut its price target to $290 Benzinga [Feb 09] CoinDesk [Feb 10].

Playbook: Own self-help stories in Europe and financials with capital-return plans; avoid consumer-exposed names into the remaining prints. Fade post-earnings bounces in crypto-linked brokers. The pattern breaks if payrolls are strong enough to revive consumer names.

Attention Gap: Henry Hub closed at 3.12, down 8.62% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10), yet the WSJ reports the US is awash in gas while American factories still can't get enough of it WSJ [Feb 10]. Data-centre and industrial demand are growing faster than the market's attention to gas.

Exposure & Risk: Express via low-cost Appalachian and Haynesville producers and gas-fired generation owners rather than front-month futures, which carry weather noise. Oil-weighted names have taken the energy flows, with XLE up 15.62% over 20 sessions while gas fell, so gas equities start from depressed expectations (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). Risk: a mild end to winter and new LNG capacity can keep prices depressed for months.

Attention Gap: Mainland investors are pouring into Hong Kong-listed drug stocks while global attention stays on China AI and chips South China Morning Post [Feb 10]. The flow is quiet but persistent, and it comes from the same southbound channel that is otherwise avoiding Hong Kong internet names.

Exposure & Risk: Use a Hong Kong biotech ETF or the large innovative drugmakers rather than single small caps. Risk: US restrictions on Chinese biotech and drug-price pressure at home; KWEB's 8.9% fall over 20 sessions shows how fast Hong Kong sentiment can turn (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

Market Context: Bitcoin's prior completed daily close was 68,793.96, down 1.89% in the prior session and 23.03% over 20 sessions, but up 9.72% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). Ether closed at 2,019.50, down 32.21%, and Solana at 82.92, down 35.91% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). IBIT closed at 38.97 and MSTR at 133.00, down 3.93% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

New / Most Important: US bitcoin ETFs registered back-to-back inflows for the first time in a month CoinDesk [Feb 10]. Michael Saylor downplayed Strategy's credit risk, saying 'we'll refinance the debt' CNBC [Feb 10]. But activity is drying up: Robinhood's revenue disappointed on a crypto slowdown Reuters [Feb 10].

Playbook: Hold a core BTC position via IBIT and add only on confirmed ETF inflows; avoid ETH and SOL, which are still underperforming bitcoin over 20 sessions. Treat Strategy as a leveraged, credit-sensitive proxy rather than a substitute for spot. Change the call if ETF inflows reverse again or Strategy's refinancing hits resistance.

Rates & Dollar: The DXY closed at 96.80, down 2.08% over 20 sessions, as the dollar weakened before payrolls on rate-cut risks (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10) Bloomberg.com [Feb 10]. The curve is in a bull steepening, with the 2Y at 3.45% and the 10Y at 4.16% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-10). TLT rose 1.15% in the prior session to 88.53 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

Credit Check: Alphabet's bond sale drew over $140b of demand for its dollar tranche, and it sold almost $32 billion of bonds in total AFR [Feb 10] Bloomberg.com [Feb 10]. HYG closed at 80.84, down 0.25% over 20 sessions, and LQD at 110.82, up 0.28% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). Investment grade is absorbing record supply; high yield is lagging slightly.

Portfolio Implication: Stay long duration at the front end and underweight the dollar into payrolls; prefer IG over HY and avoid software-exposed private credit Reuters [Feb 10]. Change the call if payrolls are strong and the DXY reclaims 98.86, its level 20 sessions ago (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

What Is Priced: The delayed January jobs report is out Wednesday CNBC [Feb 10]. The 2Y fell 12 bps over five observations to 3.45% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-10), and the dollar weakened before the report as traders weighed rate-cut risks Bloomberg.com [Feb 10]. The White House is preparing the ground for a weak number The New York Times [Feb 10].

Conditional Expression: Weak payrolls: add 2Y Treasuries, gold and small caps, with IWM at 266.16 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). Strong payrolls: the 2Y retraces toward 3.54% and the dollar rebounds; rotate from REITs and utilities back into financials and energy (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-10).

Risk: A split or ambiguous ruling could leave the legal risk open for months, which is worse for valuations than a clear outcome. After the five-session pullback in PKO BP, a benign ruling could produce a sharp relief move.
